sentiment.rationale: The document reports a strong quarter with net income of $4.1B, up 21% YoY, and revenues up 3% YoY. However, full-year 2025 guidance is reaffirmed unchanged, not raised, and management explicitly flags 'uncertainty and deterioration in the macroeconomic outlook' as a driver of an ACL build. The positive operating momentum across businesses is genuine, but the unchanged guidance and cautious forward language on credit costs and macro conditions prevent a higher score. The score of 0.15 reflects the operational momentum without a formal guidance raise.

summary.revenue: Total revenues, net of interest expense of $21,596 million for 1Q25, up 3% from $21,016 million in 1Q24.
summary.eps: Diluted earnings per share of $1.96, up from $1.58 in 1Q24, an increase of 24%.
summary.guidance: Full year 2025 guidance unchanged: revenues ~$83.1-84.1 billion, expenses slightly below $53.4 billion, NII ex-Markets up 2-3%. Subject to macro and market conditions.
summary.margin: Efficiency ratio of 62.2% for 1Q25, improved by 490 bps YoY from 67.1% in 1Q24. Return on average tangible common equity (RoTCE) of 9.1%, up 150 bps from 7.6% in 1Q24.
key_risks: Higher cost of credit: total cost of credit of $2.7 billion increased 15% YoY, driven by higher net credit losses in card portfolios and a net ACL build related to deterioration in the macroeconomic outlook.
Uncertainty and deterioration in the macroeconomic outlook: management explicitly cites this as a driver of the ACL build and notes it is subject to changing conditions.
Higher net credit losses in USPB card portfolios: NCLs in Branded Cards and Retail Services increased, with NCL rates at 3.89% and 6.43% respectively.
Decline in All Other revenues: All Other (managed basis) revenues decreased 39% YoY, driven by lower NII, mark-to-market valuation changes on investments, and Mexican peso depreciation.
Geopolitical and macroeconomic uncertainties: forward-looking statements reference risks including tariffs, inflation, unemployment, and slowing economic growth.
key_opportunities: Growth across five interconnected businesses: Services recorded best first quarter revenue in a decade; Markets revenue up 12% YoY; Banking up 12% YoY; Wealth up 24% YoY; USPB up 2% YoY.
Market share gains in Services: TTS gained ~65 bps of market share YoY; Securities Services gained ~100 bps of market share YoY.
Investment Banking wallet share gains: IB fees up 14% YoY, increased market share by ~80 bps YoY, Advisory fees up 84% YoY.
Wealth momentum: Client investment assets up 16% YoY, NNIA of $16.5B representing 11% organic growth.
Capital return to shareholders: Returned ~$2.8 billion in common dividends and share repurchases in 1Q25, with a $20 billion buyback program authorized.

management_tone.label: confident
